column5: Joseph's imprisoned cupbearer squeezes grapes
column6: The commentary puts squeezing beside detention in Joseph's prison; the cupbearer presses grapes into Pharaoh's cup inside his prison dream, giving that pairing a concrete narrative scene.

column5: cupbearer released after three days
column6: The commentary moves from prison's restraint to relief; Joseph tells the imprisoned cupbearer he will be restored to service, a specific release following the pressing dream.

column5: seven years of abundance
column6: The commentary's year of provision follows Joseph's prediction; Joseph announces years of plenty before scarcity, making productive time something to preserve.

column5: seven years of famine
column6: The commentary pairs the fruitful year with threatened loss; Joseph says famine will consume the prior abundance, turning accumulated yield into a question of survival.

column5: food stored against famine
column6: The commentary's rain, pressing and rescue culminate in usable provision; Joseph proposes keeping grain so the land will not perish in famine.

column5: Joseph promises food during famine
column6: The commentary makes Joseph's good year a deliverance for people; Joseph promises to sustain his family through the remaining famine years.

column5: sow wind and reap whirlwind
column6: The commentary's fruitful garden is erased by a whirlwind at the point of yield; Hosea makes a whirlwind the harvest of a disastrous sowing, linking crop and loss in one image.

column5: fruitful vine uprooted and dried by east wind
column6: The commentary's planted fruit is destroyed after growth by a violent wind; Ezekiel's lament uproots a fruitful vine and has the east wind dry its fruit.

column5: death on the night stored goods seem secure
column6: The commentary's old gardener loses a lifetime's yield when it should become useful; the rich fool is called to die just after planning to store his crop, and the question asks who receives it.

column5: loose bonds and free oppressed people
column6: The commentary explains the hard ascent by undoing a captive's neck; Isaiah defines the chosen fast by undoing unjust bonds and sending the oppressed free.

column5: share bread with hungry and shelter poor
column6: The commentary places feeding on a day of hunger after release; Isaiah immediately pairs liberation with sharing bread with hungry people and bringing the homeless in.

column5: proclaim release to captives
column6: The commentary makes the steep ascent an act of releasing the held person; Jesus' synagogue reading announces release to captives and freedom for the oppressed.

column5: feeding hungry and receiving stranger
column6: The commentary's difficult path includes feeding during hunger; the king identifies food given to the hungry and welcome to the stranger as acts done for him.

column5: prison visitation beside bodily care
column6: The commentary holds release, hunger and communal help in one walk; the king names visiting him in prison beside clothing the naked and caring for sickness.

column5: remember prisoners as fellow prisoners
column6: The commentary turns the captive's release into shared responsibility; Hebrews asks readers to remember prisoners as though imprisoned with them.

column5: men haul Jeremiah from a pit with ropes
column6: The commentary's road joins a burden, holding and release; Ebed-melech's men pull Jeremiah up with ropes from confinement in a cistern, a literal collective rescue.

column5: companion lifts the fallen
column6: The commentary changes a solitary difficult ascent into mutual support; Ecclesiastes says one companion raises the other after a fall.

column5: threefold cord withstands rupture
column6: The commentary's rope joins grasping, company and rescue from an edge; Ecclesiastes' cord of three strands makes solidarity itself resistant to breaking.

column5: trust like a spider's web
column6: The commentary sets the spider house against real refuge; Bildad describes the godless person's confidence as a spider's web, making apparently woven support precarious.

column5: house fails when leaned upon
column6: The commentary's spider house is a false shelter; Bildad says the godless person leans on his house but it does not stand, carrying the web image into failed reliance.

column5: spider webs cannot become clothing
column6: The commentary opposes the spider's weaving to secure covering; Isaiah says woven webs cannot cover their makers, while their deeds are violent.

column5: rain, floods and wind bring down a house
column6: The commentary's shelter image fails under destructive weather; Jesus' house built on sand collapses when rain, floods and wind strike it.

column5: dying Jacob binds Joseph by oath
column6: The commentary's testament scene unites death, custody and sworn duty; dying Jacob requires Joseph's pledged hand and loyal burial promise.

column5: two witnesses establish a matter
column6: The commentary's deathbed testament weighs witnesses and the truer claim; Deuteronomy requires two or three witnesses for a matter to stand.

column5: false sworn witnesses cause Naboth's death
column6: The commentary's testament scene makes truth in testimony decisive; two men testify falsely against Naboth and he is killed, showing the stakes of a corrupt witness.

column5: death required in a testament argument
column6: The commentary combines death and entrusted last instructions; Hebrews treats a testament as requiring the death of its maker in its covenant argument.

column5: testament operative after death
column6: The commentary's bequest becomes urgent at death; Hebrews says a testament takes effect upon death, sharpening the relation between dying and transfer.

column5: creditor must not enter debtor's house for pledge
column6: The commentary joins marketplace debt with custody of an entrusted thing; Deuteronomy restrains the lender's power over a pledged object.

column5: return pledged cloak before sunset
column6: The commentary's debt meets the passing day and the duty to return what was held; the lender must give back the poor debtor's cloak by sunset so he can sleep in it.

column5: debtor's bed taken for lack of payment
column6: The commentary imagines capital eroding and security forfeited in a bad transaction; Proverbs asks why a guarantor would risk having even his bed seized.

column5: master releases debtor and cancels loan
column6: The commentary puts restraint, debt and release in one scene; the master lets a servant go and forgives an unpayable debt.

column5: forgiven debtor seizes his debtor by the throat
column6: The commentary's holding image collides with a debt transaction; a newly forgiven servant physically grips another servant and demands repayment.

column5: unmerciful creditor jails debtor
column6: The commentary joins debt, confinement and the choice to release; the servant instead casts his fellow servant into prison until payment.

column5: Esau sells his birthright
column6: The commentary's bad purchase exchanges lasting value for ruinous immediate gain; Esau swears away his birthright for the meal offered by Jacob.

column5: Esau trades birthright for one meal
column6: The commentary's bad bargain spends enduring capital on brief satisfaction; Hebrews uses Esau's single meal as the warning's concrete transaction.

column5: profit whole world and forfeit life
column6: The commentary calls the human being a trader whose principal is lost; Jesus asks what profit remains if gaining the world costs one's life.

column5: scarlet cord marks a house for rescue
column6: The commentary's rope combines attachment with group safety at a deadly edge; Rahab is told to bind a scarlet cord in the window and gather her family in the house.

column5: family must remain inside the cord-marked house
column6: The commentary moves from individual grasp to shared safety; Rahab's household is safe within the marked house but not if members go outside.

column5: bear one another's burdens
column6: The commentary's steep path becomes a shared journey with a load; Paul commands the community to carry one another's burdens.

column5: exhort one another every day
column6: The commentary reads the last verse as reciprocal transfer across passing time; Hebrews commands daily mutual exhortation so no one hardens through sin.

column5: consider how to stir love and good works
column6: The commentary passes counsel into fitting deeds within a group; Hebrews asks people to consider one another so love and good works result.

column5: assemble and encourage as the day approaches
column6: The commentary's people preserve each other through diminishing time toward a decisive day; Hebrews connects gathering, mutual encouragement and the approaching day.

column5: encourage and build each other up
column6: The commentary says people fit together like building material and pass counsel between them; Paul tells them to encourage one another and build each other up.

column5: admonish, help weak and be patient with all
column6: The commentary pairs reciprocal advice with patience and care for vulnerable people; Paul joins these commands in one instruction to the community.

column5: entrust teaching to people who will teach others
column6: The commentary's truth and patience are handed onward and kept; Timothy must entrust received teaching to reliable people able to teach still others.

column5: guard the entrusted good deposit
column6: The commentary ends with an essence kept and passed rather than spent; Timothy is ordered to guard a received deposit through the Holy Spirit.

column5: patient farmer waits for precious crop and rains
column6: The commentary ties patience to rain, fruit, useful yield and passing time; James makes a farmer waiting for rains and harvest the model for patient endurance.

column5: hold word and bear fruit with endurance
column6: The commentary joins holding, fruitful work and sabr as kept substance; Jesus' good soil consists of hearers who hold the word and bear fruit through endurance.

column5: endurance, commandments and faith together
column6: The commentary closes with faith, right deeds and patience held by a people; Revelation calls for the endurance of saints who keep God's commands and faith in Jesus.

column5: captivity and endurance of the saints
column6: The commentary makes holding and captivity meet patience; Revelation speaks of captivity and immediately names the endurance and faith of the saints.

column5: weighed in scales and found wanting
column6: The commentary pairs severed supports with light weight in the final balance; Daniel's verdict on Belshazzar finds him deficient when weighed.

column5: ancestry from Abraham cannot be assumed as security
column6: The commentary imagines lineage severed before assessment; John warns his hearers that claiming Abraham as father will not secure their standing.

column5: dead judged by written record of works
column6: The commentary moves from broken lineage and light scales to a day confronting each person with deeds; the dead stand for judgment according to what is recorded of their works.

column5: wealth useless on day of wrath
column6: The commentary's spent principal meets the day that exposes what remains; Proverbs says riches cannot help on the day of wrath, whereas righteousness delivers.

column5: each repaid according to deeds
column6: The commentary's truth includes a day that faces everyone with their work; Paul says God renders to each person according to deeds.

column5: speak truth to neighbour and judge truly
column6: The commentary treats haqq as a thing passed mutually and as a sound verdict; Zechariah commands true speech to neighbours and truthful judgment at the gates.

column5: speak truth to neighbour because members belong together
column6: The commentary shifts from the lone human to a mutually bound group handing on truth; Paul grounds truthful speech in shared membership.

column5: doing truth brings deeds into light
column6: The commentary joins truth with rightly placed works; John says the one who does truth comes to light so that the deeds done in God become visible.

column5: painful discipline later yields righteous fruit
column6: The commentary treats patience as a bitter essence preserved for benefit; Hebrews says discipline hurts now yet later yields peaceful fruit of righteousness.

column5: faithful friend's wounds
column6: The commentary imagines true counsel as an unpleasant medicine retained for good; Proverbs values the wounds of a faithful friend over an enemy's plentiful kisses.

column5: painful sorrow leads to repentance and rescue
column6: The commentary's bitter retained counsel serves endurance rather than waste; Paul distinguishes godly sorrow that produces repentance and salvation from sorrow that produces death.

column5: living stones built into one house
column6: The commentary likens fitting good works and joined believers to building blocks; Peter describes believers as living stones being built into a spiritual house.

column5: people built together into a dwelling
column6: The commentary says individuals fit into one community like placed bricks; Paul says his addressees are built together into a dwelling for God.

column5: rain supports grain, wine and oil
column6: The commentary's garden links rain to produce that can be pressed; Deuteronomy promises seasonal rain so grain, wine and oil can be gathered, without Joseph's explicit rescue scene.

column5: threshing floors full and vats overflow
column6: The commentary's good side of the year is stored produce and pressing; Joel imagines restored abundance filling floors with grain and vats with wine and oil.

column5: years consumed by locusts restored
column6: The commentary pictures a lifetime's accumulated crop erased; Joel answers lost productive years with a promise to restore what successive locust swarms consumed.

column5: vineyard deprived of rain after judgment
column6: The commentary's rain-grown garden can be lost in a single turn; Isaiah's judged vineyard is denied rain after its owner abandons its care, a reversed weather detail.

column5: barns enlarged to store harvest
column6: The commentary treats late accumulated fruit as vulnerable capital; the rich fool builds larger barns for all his grain and goods just before the death sentence in Luke 12:20.

column5: planned profitable future cut short by brief life
column6: The commentary locates human loss inside spent time; James challenges merchants planning another trading year by saying they cannot know tomorrow and life is a vapour.

column5: work burns and builder suffers loss
column6: The commentary sees a lifetime's work destroyed just when its value is tested; Paul says a builder whose work burns suffers loss though he himself is saved.

column5: freed servant must not leave empty-handed
column6: The commentary's steep path joins release with practical provision; Deuteronomy says a freed servant must not be sent away empty-handed.

column5: provision from flock, threshing floor and winepress
column6: The commentary links freeing a captive with feeding and pressed yield; Deuteronomy orders gifts from animals, grain and winepress to the departing servant.

column5: words of blessing without food fail hungry people
column6: The commentary's mutual exhortation follows the actual feeding of the hungry; James exposes a verbal blessing that supplies neither clothing nor daily food.

column5: traveller lifts wounded man onto his animal
column6: The commentary's hard road includes a beast, a burden and practical rescue; the Samaritan treats the injured man and carries him on his own animal to shelter.

column5: resources distributed by need
column6: The commentary's community exchanges what preserves others after loss; the Jerusalem group lays sale proceeds before the apostles for distribution according to need.

column5: Joseph's burial oath entrusted to descendants
column6: The commentary's testament binds witnesses and future custodians across death; Joseph makes Israelites swear to carry his bones when God brings them out.

column5: true witness saves lives
column6: The commentary's testament scene weighs truthful against corrupt testimony; Proverbs says a truthful witness delivers lives while a deceitful witness speaks lies.

column5: two or three witnesses establish the matter
column6: The commentary asks which testimony is truer after a contested bequest; Jesus directs a dispute to witnesses so a matter can be established.

column5: simple yes and no instead of elaborate oaths
column6: The commentary's testament scene needs a formal oath to safeguard disputed truth; Jesus demands plain truthful speech beyond oath formulas, a deliberate contrast in how assurance is secured.

column5: record of debt cancelled
column6: The commentary joins debt, entrustment and release; Paul depicts a hostile written record of obligations as cancelled and removed, extending the debt image to deliverance.

column5: bought with a price, do not become slaves
column6: The commentary's ascent connects market exchange to freedom from bondage; Paul uses purchase language to forbid renewed human enslavement.

column5: buy truth and do not sell it
column6: The commentary places truth beside the bad bargain where lasting value is spent; Proverbs makes truth something to acquire and keep rather than trade away.

column5: spend wages on what fails to nourish
column6: The commentary's human loses principal through a false purchase; Isaiah asks why people spend money on what is not bread and labour on what does not satisfy.

column5: divine patience waits while ark is built
column6: The commentary's patience holds life secure while a weak refuge fails; Peter recalls divine patience during ark construction before the flood, linking endurance to a built shelter.

column5: storing wrath for judgment day
column6: The commentary contrasts keeping a life-giving essence with buying fire through stubbornness; Paul says an unrepentant heart stores wrath for the coming day.

column5: wicked people weave spider webs
column6: The commentary contrasts useful weaving with the spider's false house; Isaiah names spider webs among the works produced by violent, deceitful people.

column5: wise builder sets house on rock
column6: The commentary's spider house is a failed shelter; Jesus' hearer who acts on his words makes a sound house on rock, supplying the constructive counterpart to the storm's collapse.

column5: Rahab's family brought out together
column6: The commentary links a cord to collective escape from the edge; Joshua's scouts bring Rahab and her whole family out when the city falls, completing the cord-marked rescue of Joshua 2:18.

column5: unity kept by bond of peace
column6: The commentary's common grasp replaces enmity with brotherhood; Paul urges the community to maintain the Spirit's unity in the bond of peace.

column5: community restores someone caught in a fault
column6: The commentary's group saves a person from a figurative edge through shared counsel; Paul tells spiritually mature members to restore the person caught in transgression gently.

column5: bring wanderer back from ruin
column6: The commentary's reciprocal advice prevents a fall into loss; James says turning a sinner from a wandering path saves a soul from death.

column5: people of day rather than night
column6: The commentary likens members of the final community to night and day arranged together; Paul calls his audience children of light and of day, giving the adjacent exhortation in 1 Thessalonians 5:11 a temporal setting.

column5: teach and admonish one another
column6: The commentary's final verse passes haqq through reciprocal counsel; Paul asks the word to dwell in the group as members teach and admonish each other.

column5: entrusted deposit kept until that day
column6: The commentary connects keeping an entrusted essence with the day that reveals deeds; Paul says the one he trusts can guard his deposit until that day.

column5: truth heard, belief followed by sealing
column6: The commentary joins faith, transmitted truth and the image of a sealed store; Paul says believers heard the word of truth, believed and were sealed with the promised Spirit.

column5: seal and guarantee placed in hearts
column6: The commentary gives sabr the secondary sense of guarantor and sealed contents; Paul depicts God sealing believers and giving the Spirit as a guarantee in their hearts.

column5: just balance for moral assessment
column6: The commentary's loss is pictured as being light on a scale; Job invites God to weigh him on an honest balance to know his integrity.

column5: child does not carry parent's guilt
column6: The commentary sets severed genealogical ties beside individual weighing; Ezekiel denies transfer of a father's guilt to a son, making personal conduct decisive.

column5: obedience defines kinship
column6: The commentary shifts from ancestry that fails to a community formed by deeds; Jesus calls those who do his Father's will his brother, sister and mother.

column5: coming day discloses hidden motives
column6: The commentary's haqq is the day when each person confronts what was done; Paul says the Lord will bring hidden things to light and disclose the intentions of hearts.

column5: painful letter causes useful grief
column6: The commentary's preserved bitter medicine is corrective speech; Paul admits his letter grieved its recipients, then treats the short grief as part of their recovery.

column5: false oath prohibited among neighbours
column6: The commentary's bequest joins oath and truth with reciprocal duty; Zechariah forbids loving false oaths as part of the same neighbourly justice expressed in Zechariah 8:16.

column5: patience is fruit borne by a community
column6: The commentary ends with patience kept as an enduring yield; Paul includes patience among the Spirit's fruit alongside love and peace.

column5: bricks made for collective city project
column6: The commentary's believers fit together like sound bricks for helpful works; Babel's people likewise make bricks together, but their shared building becomes a project of self-exaltation and dispersal.
